text: dsh-omni-workstation 是面向 DSH Web 与 CLI 的多模态工作站插件，通过注册 AI 工具、设置面板和视频构建命令接入。它可分析图片，提供缩放、取色、对比、OCR 和元素检测等视觉工具，生成图片与视频，并提供语音合成、音色克隆和转写。适合需要在 DSH 会话中处理图像、视频或语音的用户；远程模型功能需在配置中设置相应服务。

dsh-omni-workstation is a multimodal plugin for DSH web and CLI. It adds AI tools, a settings panel, and a video builder. It analyzes images, generates images and videos, and supports speech, voice cloning, and transcription.
想让 DSH 看懂我发的图片并回答问题。
有没有办法在会话里直接生成图片并存到项目目录？
我想比较两张图片的差异并看出主要颜色。
能不能让 DSH 把一段文字转换成语音？
I want to transcribe an audio file from my DSH session.
Can I build a custom video-generation tool for a provider I use?
dsh-omni-workstation 的功能「图片问答」：分析本地或上传的图片并回答问题。AI 调用 analyze_image 工具，输入图片路径或附件标识和问题，得到模型分析结果。
dsh-omni-workstation 的功能「图像生成」：根据提示词生成图片，可选参考图片和输出目录。AI 调用 generate_image，生成结果以文件路径返回。
dsh-omni-workstation 的功能「图像工具箱」：可缩放图片、提取主色、比较差异、识别文字和检测元素。AI 调用对应视觉工具，输入图片及选项，得到文字、颜色或检测结果；部分操作会保存图像工件。
dsh-omni-workstation 的功能「语音工具」：提供文本转语音、音色克隆和音频转写。AI 调用 speak、clone_voice 或 transcribe，传入文本、音色或音频输入，获得音频文件、音色信息或转写文本。
dsh-omni-workstation 使用前须知：图片分析会把图片内容交给所选的视觉模型服务处理；具体目标由配置的服务商决定。（见 lib/index.js:2963-2995、lib/client.js:73）

想在 DSH 里克隆音色，再用它朗读文本。

dsh-omni-workstation README · dsh-omni-workstation：An **omni-modal workstation plugin** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (`dsh`). It gives the AI eyes, a brush, a camera and a voice: image analysis backed by an ordered multi-card VLM failover chain, a 6-tool local vision toolkit, image generation (incl. ComfyUI workflows), multi-card async video generation with an AI tool builder, and TTS / voice cloning across 3 cloud + 4 local providers — all configured from one auto-saving settings page (English / 中文).

dsh-omni-workstation README · Install：The plugin is a **bundle**: it carries its own `cordis.patch.yml` and self-activates — one command, no manual patch editing.

```bash
dsh-omni-workstation README · From a local directory：dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-omni-workstation
dsh-omni-workstation README · From GitHub：dsh plugin --profile web add github:huashenglian/dsh-omni-workstation

dsh-omni-workstation README · From a packed tarball (pnpm pack / npm pack)：dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-omni-workstation-0.2.0-beta.1.tgz
```

`dsh plugin add` installs the dependency and appends the bundle to `dsh.profile.bundles` automatically.

> [!NOTE]bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

dsh-omni-workstation README · Requirements：- `dsh` CLI (DeepSeek Harness) with a `web` profile — or any CLI/headless profile (see [CLI / headless](#cli--headless-no-browser))
- `pnpm` on `PATH` (or use `npx --yes pnpm@<version>`)

dsh-omni-workstation README · Quick Start：1. Restart `dsh web` and open **Settings → Omni Workstation**.
2. On the VLM tab, click **Add Model** (or edit the default card): pick a provider, paste your API key, fetch and pick a model.
3. Send the AI an image (or a local path) and ask about it — the `analyze_image` tool is now live.

dsh-omni-workstation README · Configuration：All settings live in **one JSON file**, `omni-vision.json`. The settings page writes it, and in a terminal-only setup it is the *only* way to configure the plugin — there are no extra slash commands to memorize.

**Where the file lives** (highest priority first):

dsh-omni-workstation README · Configuration：| # | Path | When it is used |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `$DSH_OMNI_WORKSTATION_CONFIG_DIR/omni-vision.json` | test / advanced override only |
| 2 | `~/.dsh/omni-vision.json` — or `$DSH_HOME/omni-vision.json` when `DSH_HOME` is set | **recommended**; used whenever it exists, and the default target for a new install |
| 3 | `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-omni-workstation/omni-vision.json` | legacy location (v2.5–v2.13); still honoured while no home file exists |

dsh-omni-workstation README · Configuration：On Windows: `C:\Users\<you>\.dsh\omni-vision.json`. Everything the plugin persists lives **next to that file**: `omni-vision.json.bak` (recovery copy), `omni-vision.schema.json` (editor completion), `voice-library/` (cloned voice samples) and `transcripts/` (STT output).

dsh-omni-workstation README · Configuration：> [!TIP]
> - **Hand edits apply without a restart.** The plugin re-reads the file on the next agent step and re-registers tools accordingly.
> - The boot log prints the resolved path and which modules are live, e.g. `[dsh-omni-workstation] config: /home/you/.dsh/omni-vision.json (home) | vlm=on(2 cards) toolkit=on …`. Check it if you are unsure which file is in use.
> - A JSON syntax error is reported with the path and **never overwrites your file** — the plugin keeps running on the last good `.bak` (in memory) until you fix it.
> - The file holds real API keys: never commit it. The plugin writes `"$schema": "omni-vision.schema.json"` on every save, which gives editor autocomplete + validation; add that single line yourself only if you created the file outside the plugin (see [configuration reference](docs/reference/configuration.md)).
> - Moving a legacy config to the stable location: `cp ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-omni-workstation/omni-vision.json ~/.dsh/` (PowerShell: `Copy-Item <src> ~/.dsh/omni-vision.json`). The home file wins from then on.

dsh-omni-workstation README · add one valid VLM card to ~/.dsh/omni-vision.json (see above), then:：- `analyze_image`, the 6 vision tools, `generate_image` / `generate_video`, `speak` / `clone_voice` / `transcribe` all work — each gated by the same switches in the config file.
- Browser-only extras: the settings page itself, the `/omni/*` HTTP routes, the in-chat visual preview rendered by `show_image` / `show_video` (the tools still work and return artifact paths) and the `/build-video-tool` slash command.
- Web and CLI profiles read the **same** file, so you configure once and use it everywhere.

dsh-omni-workstation README · Feature Overview：| Module | Tool | Highlights |
|---|---|---|
| [VLM](docs/features/vlm.md) | `analyze_image` | Ordered API card list, single-request failover, per-card timeout, JPEG→PNG fallback, 28 built-in providers, mirror models, dynamic multimodal adaptation |
| [Vision Toolkit](docs/features/vision-toolkit.md) | `zoom_image` · `sample_colors` · `image_diff` · `ocr_image` · `detect_elements` · `show_image` | 4 tools are pure-local (zero tokens); shared image resolution + card chain; artifact paths only |
| [Image Gen](docs/features/imggen.md) | `generate_image` | OpenAI / DashScope / ComfyUI protocols, multi-workflow management with role mapping, reference-image support, auto verify reminder |
| [Video](docs/features/video.md) | `generate_video` (+ per-card names) | Multi-card (limit 10), 7 protocols, `/build-video-tool` AI builder with `custom-adapter` runtime |
| [Voice](docs/features/voice.md) | `speak` · `clone_voice` · `transcribe` | MiMo / MiniMax / Doubao + IndexTTS / GPT-SoVITS / VoxCPM / TTS-WebUI; zero-registration inline & persisted cloning; speech-to-text via one OpenAI-compatible protocol (local FunASR by default, no key needed) |

dsh-omni-workstation README · Feature Overview：Every module has its own switch (on by default, except the STT sub-switch), but a switch alone is not enough: turning one off unregisters its tools completely, and an incomplete configuration never registers the tool at all (0 token cost) while keeping your configuration.

dsh-omni-workstation README · Why a plugin instead of a Skill or a fixed script：| Approach | Typical pain | What this plugin does |
|---|---|---|
| Long Skill text (official-API recipes) | A big instruction dump every turn — expensive tokens | Config lives only in the settings page / `omni-vision.json`; tool schemas inject only when a module is on |
| Fixed scripts (hand-written API calls) | Locked in a project folder; you must restate path and usage each time | Tools register into the harness — the AI finds and reuses them automatically |
| Changing config / switching models | Edit scripts or re-paste the Skill body | Change a field in Settings; it takes effect immediately |
section: Why a plugin instead of a Skill or a fixed script

text: dsh-omni-workstation README · Custom tools (video)：Today you can AI-build a **custom video tool**: type `/build-video-tool` in chat. The plugin injects a build guide (card limit, existing tools, hard constraints); the AI collects the platform details and writes a new card plus a callable tool — no hand-written script, no re-pasting API docs.

dsh-omni-workstation README · Custom tools (video)：> [!TIP]
> Card limit defaults to 10; the command errors out when the cap is hit. Custom tools run on the `custom-adapter` runtime — see the [video docs](docs/features/video.md).
dsh-omni-workstation README · Settings Panel：

dsh-omni-workstation README · Settings Panel：**Settings → Omni Workstation** — four tabs (VLM / Image Gen / Video / Voice) plus a global settings tab. Every edit auto-saves and takes effect immediately; no Save button.

dsh-omni-workstation README · How It Works：- **Host half** (`lib/index.js`) — a cordis plugin: registers tools on the global tools registry, loads and persists `omni-vision.json` (see [Configuration](#configuration)), and re-syncs registration on config changes — including changes made by hand while it runs. The `/omni/*` web routes are registered only where a `webServer` exists (web / desktop compositions); CLI and headless compositions get the tools without any HTTP surface.
- **Client half** (`lib/client.js`) — the browser module (loaded via the `dsh.client` entry): registers the **Settings → Omni Workstation** section and its locale namespace (`settings.omni-workstation`).

dsh-omni-workstation README · Uninstall：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-omni-workstation
```

This removes the dependency and the bundle entry. A config at `~/.dsh/omni-vision.json` **survives** (delete it manually if you want the API keys gone); a legacy config inside the plugin directory is removed together with the plugin.
